input.text: Setup (s1): I(a, b) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} dx / ((x^2 + a^2)*(x^2 + b^2)) for real a > 0, b > 0. Positivity fixes the upper-half-plane poles at z = +i*a and z = +i*b and removes absolute values.

input.code:
import sympy as sp
x = sp.Symbol('x', real=True)
z = sp.Symbol('z')
a, b = sp.symbols('a b', positive=True)
integrand = 1 / ((x**2 + a**2)*(x**2 + b**2))
pf = (1/(b**2 - a**2)) * (1/(x**2 + a**2) - 1/(x**2 + b**2))
assert sp.simplify(integrand - pf) == 0
f_z = 1 / ((z**2 + a**2)*(z**2 + b**2))
res_ia = sp.simplify(sp.residue(f_z, z, sp.I*a))
res_ib = sp.simplify(sp.residue(f_z, z, sp.I*b))
I_res = sp.simplify(2*sp.pi*sp.I*(res_ia + res_ib))
I_cf = sp.pi / (a*b*(a + b))
assert sp.simplify(I_res - I_cf) == 0
I_pf = sp.simplify((1/(b**2 - a**2))*(sp.integrate(1/(x**2 + a**2), (x, -sp.oo, sp.oo)) - sp.integrate(1/(x**2 + b**2), (x, -sp.oo, sp.oo))))
assert sp.simplify(I_pf - I_cf) == 0
print('Distinct poles a != b verified:', I_res)

import sympy as sp
x = sp.Symbol('x', real=True)
z = sp.Symbol('z')
a, b = sp.symbols('a b', positive=True)
I_cf = sp.pi / (a*b*(a + b))
f_deg = 1 / (z**2 + a**2)**2
res_deg = sp.simplify(sp.residue(f_deg, z, sp.I*a))
I_deg_res = sp.simplify(2*sp.pi*sp.I*res_deg)
I_deg_lim = sp.limit(I_cf, b, a, '+')
I_deg_direct = sp.integrate(1/(x**2 + a**2)**2, (x, -sp.oo, sp.oo))
assert sp.simplify(I_deg_res - sp.pi/(2*a**3)) == 0
assert sp.simplify(I_deg_lim - sp.pi/(2*a**3)) == 0
assert sp.simplify(I_deg_direct - sp.pi/(2*a**3)) == 0
I_direct = sp.simplify(sp.integrate(1/((x**2 + a**2)*(x**2 + b**2)), (x, -sp.oo, sp.oo)))
assert sp.simplify(I_direct - I_cf) == 0
print('Degenerate b = a and direct integral verified:', I_deg_res, I_direct)

content.text:
For real a > 0 and b > 0, closing the contour in the upper half-plane encloses the poles at z = +i*a and z = +i*b (simple when a != b, double when b = a). Positivity a > 0, b > 0 ensures these lie in Im(z) > 0 and removes absolute values (otherwise |a| and |b| appear). Both the distinct-pole residue sum and the continuous limit b -> a+ (matching the double-pole value pi/(2*a^3)) yield the uniform closed form:

pi/(a*b*(a + b))
